app.name.note: The product name, in the browser tab and in e-mails. Not translated.

sign-in.title.note: The sign-in page's heading and browser tab title. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

sign-in.passkey.note: Button that signs in with a passkey, shown first where the browser supports passkeys (ADR-0011 §6).

sign-in.or-password.note: Leads from the passkey button to the e-mail and password form below it.

sign-in.passkey-failed.note: When signing in with a passkey was cancelled or refused. Calm: the password still works.

sign-in.email.note: Label of the e-mail address field on the sign-in page.

sign-in.password.note: Label of the password field on the sign-in page.

sign-in.failed.note: Heading of the box at the top of the sign-in page that says why signing in didn't work.

sign-in.incorrect.note: After a sign-in with a wrong e-mail address or password. It never says which, so it doesn't reveal whether an address has an account (ADR-0010 §2).

sign-in.unverified.note: After a sign-in with the right password, to an account whose e-mail address hasn't been confirmed with the link we e-mailed.

sign-in.wait-seconds.note: After repeated failed sign-ins, the next attempt has to wait (ADR-0010 §2). {count} is the number of seconds. Calm and factual: it never blames.

sign-in.wait-minutes.note: As sign-in.wait-seconds, for waits of a minute or more. {count} is the number of minutes, rounded up.

security.title.note: Heading of the security page, where a member sees and signs out their devices (ADR-0010 §6).

security.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the security page. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

security.devices.note: Heading of the list of devices the account is signed in on.

security.device.note: A signed-in device. {browser} and {system} are names such as Firefox and Android, not translated.

security.unknown-browser.note: Stands in for {browser} in security.device when the browser isn't known; starts the sentence.

security.unknown-system.note: Stands in for {system} in security.device when the operating system isn't known; mid-sentence.

security.unknown-device.note: A signed-in device whose browser and system are both unknown.

security.this-device.note: Marks the device the member is using right now in the list of signed-in devices.

security.used-today.note: When a signed-in device was last used, within the last day. Exact to a day only.

security.used-days.note: When a signed-in device was last used. {count} is whole days ago, at least 1.

security.sign-out.note: Button next to each signed-in device that signs it out; next to this device, it signs the member out here.

security.sign-out-others.note: Button that signs out every device but the one in use.

security.signed-out.note: Status message after signing out another device.

security.signed-out-others.note: Status message after signing out all other devices.

security.not-found.note: Status message when the device to sign out was signed out already, for example from another tab.

security.passkeys.note: Heading of the security page's list of passkeys (ADR-0010 §2). Passkey is the common word in both languages.

security.passkeys-intro.note: Explains what a passkey is, in one line.

security.no-passkeys.note: Shown instead of the list when the account has no passkeys.

security.added-today.note: When a passkey was added less than a day ago.

security.added-days.note: When a passkey was added, in whole days; {count} is at least 1.

security.add-passkey.note: Button that starts adding a passkey; the browser then asks for the fingerprint, face or screen lock.

security.remove-passkey.note: Button next to a passkey that removes it. Its device name is read with it.

security.passkey-added.note: Status message after a passkey was added.

security.passkey-removed.note: Status message after a passkey was removed.

security.passkey-not-found.note: Status message when the passkey to remove was already gone.

security.passkey-remove-failed.note: Heading of the box that says why a passkey wasn't removed. Same pattern as security.passkey-failed.

security.passkey-head.note: Why removing a passkey is refused: heads must keep two factors, and without this passkey they would have neither another passkey nor a password with two-factor authentication (ADR-0010 §3). Same pattern as security.two-factor-head.

security.passkey-failed.note: When the browser or the server couldn't add the passkey, for instance because it was cancelled.

security.confirm.note: Heading of the step that asks for the password again before passkeys can change (ADR-0010 §6).

security.confirm-intro.note: Why it's asked again: the sign-in is over 10 minutes old. The person confirms with a passkey, or the password (and a code from their authenticator app when two-factor is on), before passkeys or two-factor change (ADR-0010 §6).

security.confirm-passkey.note: Button that confirms it's you with one of the account's passkeys, instead of the password (ADR-0010 §6).

security.passkey-confirm-failed.note: When confirming with a passkey was cancelled or refused.

security.confirm-password.note: Label of the password field when confirming it's you.

security.confirm-submit.note: Button that confirms with the password.

security.confirm-failed.note: Heading of the box that says why confirming didn't work.

security.incorrect-password.note: When the password typed to confirm is wrong.

security.confirmed.note: Status message after confirming: passkeys and two-factor can change for 10 minutes.

security.confirm-code.note: Label of the code field when confirming it's you, shown when two-factor is on. Use the same term for 'authenticator app' everywhere.

security.incorrect-code.note: When confirming it's you: the password was right, the code wasn't.

security.two-factor.note: Heading of the security page's section about codes from an authenticator app (ADR-0010 §2). Use the same term everywhere, also in the e-mails.

security.two-factor-intro.note: What two-factor authentication does, in plain words. Only shown to accounts with a password.

security.two-factor-on.note: The section's state, and the status message once it was turned on.

security.two-factor-off.note: The section's state, and the status message once it was turned off.

security.turn-on.note: Button that starts setting up an authenticator app.

security.setup.note: Heading of the setup steps: scan the QR code or enter the key, then enter the app's first code.

security.setup-scan.note: First setup step, above the QR code.

security.setup-qr.note: What a screen reader says for the QR code image.

security.setup-key.note: Before the setup key, for typing it into the app instead of scanning. The key itself isn't translated.

security.setup-code.note: Label of the field for the app's first code, which finishes the setup.

security.setup-code-hint.note: Hint below the setup code field. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

security.setup-submit.note: Button that finishes the setup with the app's first code.

security.two-factor-failed.note: Heading of the box that says why turning two-factor on or off, or making new recovery codes, didn't work.

security.setup-incorrect.note: When the setup's first code is wrong. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

security.setup-not-started.note: When a setup code arrives but no setup waits for one, for instance after it was finished in another tab.

security.two-factor-unavailable.note: When turning it on is started while it is on already, for instance from another tab.

security.two-factor-head.note: Why turning it off is refused: heads must keep two factors (ADR-0010 §3). A passkey counts as two factors.

security.two-factor-already-off.note: When new recovery codes are asked for while two-factor is off, for instance from another tab.

security.recovery-codes.note: Heading above the ten recovery codes, shown once after turning two-factor on or making new codes (ADR-0010 §2).

security.recovery-codes-intro.note: What recovery codes are for, and that they're shown only now. Calm, no urgency beyond the fact.

security.recovery-codes-done.note: Link below the recovery codes that closes them, once they are saved.

security.new-recovery-codes.note: Button that replaces the recovery codes with ten new ones; the old ones stop working.

security.recovery-codes-made.note: Status message after making new recovery codes.

email.password-reset.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail with a link to choose a new password (ADR-0010 §8). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.password-reset.request.note: First line of the password reset e-mail. It doesn't say who asked: anyone can ask for any address.

email.password-reset.action.note: Text of the link in the password reset e-mail, and the label before the link in its plain-text part.

email.password-reset.expiry.note: Says how long the reset link works (ADR-0010 §8: once, for 30 minutes).

email.password-reset.not-you.note: Last line of the password reset e-mail, for someone who didn't ask. Calm: nothing happens unless the link is used.

email.password-changed.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent after a password was changed through a reset link (ADR-0010 §8). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.password-changed.done.note: First line of the password-changed e-mail: what happened, including that every device was signed out.

email.password-changed.not-you.note: For someone who didn't change it: their mailbox is the way in. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

email.passkey-added.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent when a passkey was added to the account (ADR-0010 §2, ADR-0014 §2). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.passkey-added.done.note: First line of the passkey-added e-mail: what happened, and what a passkey can do.

email.passkey-added.not-you.note: For someone who didn't add it: someone else is signed in. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

email.passkey-removed.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent when a passkey was removed from the account. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.passkey-removed.done.note: First line of the passkey-removed e-mail.

email.passkey-removed.not-you.note: For someone who didn't remove it. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

email.two-factor-on.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent when two-factor authentication was turned on (ADR-0010 §2, ADR-0014 §2). Householdr is the product name, not translated. Use the same term for two-factor authentication everywhere.

email.two-factor-on.done.note: First line of the two-factor-on e-mail: what happened, and what changes when signing in.

email.two-factor-on.not-you.note: For someone who didn't turn it on: someone else is signed in. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

email.two-factor-off.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent when two-factor authentication was turned off. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.two-factor-off.done.note: First line of the two-factor-off e-mail: what happened, and what it means for signing in.

email.two-factor-off.not-you.note: For someone who didn't turn it off. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

email.recovery-codes-changed.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent when new recovery codes replaced the old ones (ADR-0010 §2). Recovery codes sign in once each when the authenticator app isn't at hand. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.recovery-codes-changed.done.note: First line of the e-mail about new recovery codes.

email.recovery-codes-changed.not-you.note: For someone who didn't make new recovery codes. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

sign-in.forgot-password.note: Link on the sign-in page to ask for a password reset. The password-changed e-mail quotes it, so keep both the same.

sign-in.password-changed.note: Status message on the sign-in page after a new password was saved.

forgot.title.note: Heading of the page to ask for a link to choose a new password (ADR-0010 §8).

forgot.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the forgotten-password page. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

forgot.email.note: Label of the e-mail address field on the forgotten-password page.

forgot.submit.note: Button that asks for the reset link.

forgot.sent.note: After asking for a link. It never says whether {email}, the address typed, has an account (ADR-0010 §2).

forgot.failed.note: Heading of the box that says why asking for a link didn't work.

forgot.invalid.note: When what was typed isn't an e-mail address. The example address is an invented one.

reset.title.note: Heading of the page reached from the reset link, to choose a new password.

reset.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the new-password page. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

reset.password.note: Label of the new password field.

reset.hint.note: Hint under the new password field (ADR-0010 §2: at least 12 characters, no composition rules).

reset.submit.note: Button that saves the new password.

reset.failed.note: Heading of the box that says why saving the new password didn't work.

reset.too-short.note: When the new password has fewer than 12 characters.

reset.too-long.note: When the new password has more than 128 characters.

reset.breached.note: When the new password is in Have I Been Pwned's list of breached passwords (ADR-0010 §2). Calm: it says why, without blame.

reset.expired.note: When the reset link was used already, is older than 30 minutes, or isn't one.

reset.ask-again.note: Link to the forgotten-password page, after an expired link.

reset.code.note: Label of the one field for a code on the new-password page, shown when the account has two-factor authentication on (ADR-0010 §8). It takes a code from the app or a recovery code. Same words as sign-in-code.code and sign-in-code.recovery-code.

reset.recovery-code-hint.note: Hint below the code field on the new-password page, after sign-in-code.intro. Keep the example code as it is. Same words as sign-in-code.recovery-code-hint.

reset.needs-code.note: When the account has two-factor on and the code field was left empty.

reset.incorrect-code.note: When the code from the app or the recovery code is wrong, or was used already. Calm: it never blames.

reset.wait-seconds.note: After repeated wrong codes, the next attempt has to wait (ADR-0010 §2). "This" is saving the new password with a code. {count} is the number of seconds. Calm and factual: it never blames.

reset.wait-minutes.note: As reset.wait-seconds, for waits of a minute or more. {count} is the number of minutes, rounded up.

sign-in.create-household.note: Link from the sign-in page to signing up, which creates a household (ADR-0010 §1).

sign-in-code.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the step after a right password, which asks for a code (ADR-0010 §2). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

sign-in-code.title.note: Heading of the step that asks for a code after the password. Use the same term as security.two-factor.

sign-in-code.intro.note: What to do on the code step. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

sign-in-code.code.note: Label of the code field on the code step. Same words as security.confirm-code.

sign-in-code.submit.note: Button that signs in with the app's code. Same words as sign-in.submit.

sign-in-code.use-recovery-code.note: Opens the field for a recovery code, for when the authenticator app isn't at hand.

sign-in-code.recovery-code.note: Label of the recovery code field.

sign-in-code.recovery-code-hint.note: Hint below the recovery code field. Keep the example code as it is.

sign-in-code.recovery-submit.note: Button that signs in with a recovery code.

sign-in-code.incorrect.note: When the app's code is wrong, or was used already.

sign-in-code.incorrect-recovery.note: When the recovery code is wrong or used up.

sign-in-code.expired.note: When the step after the password is over: 10 minutes passed, or it was used. Not the person's fault.

sign-in-code.start-again.note: Link back to the sign-in page, to enter the password again.

sign-up.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the sign-up page. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

sign-up.title.note: Heading of the sign-up page: signing up creates a household; the other way in is an invitation (ADR-0010 §1).

sign-up.intro.note: Under the heading: signing up starts by confirming the e-mail address with a link (ADR-0010 §1, clarification).

sign-up.email.note: Label of the e-mail address field.

sign-up.submit.note: Button that asks for the link.

sign-up.sent.note: Status after asking for a link. The same for every address, so it never shows whether one has an account (ADR-0010 §2); an address with an account gets no e-mail (§1, clarification).

sign-up.failed.note: Heading of the error summary when asking for a link failed.

sign-up.invalid.note: When what was typed isn't an e-mail address.

sign-up.wait.note: When 10 sign-ups came from the same network within an hour (ADR-0017 §5, clarification). Calm: no blame, nothing about any address.

sign-up.have-account.note: Link to the sign-in page, for someone who already has an account.

household-setup.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the first step of setting up a household (ADR-0007 §2). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

household-setup.title.note: Heading of the first step of setting up a household, reached through the sign-up link (ADR-0007 §2).

household-setup.confirmed.note: Says that the address the link was sent to is confirmed. {email} is that address.

household-setup.expired.note: When the sign-up link was used already, is older than 30 minutes, or isn't one.

household-setup.ask-again.note: Link to the sign-up page, after an expired link.

household-setup.intro.note: Under the heading of the first step of setting up a household (ADR-0007 §2). The household's settings, and the head's name and language, can all be changed later.

household-setup.household.note: Heading of the group of the household's own fields: its name, country, time zone, language and week start day.

household-setup.household-name.note: Label of the household's name field, such as a family name or a street. Everyone in the household sees it.

household-setup.country.note: Label of the household's country, one of the EU and the EEA (ADR-0016 §1), filled in from the browser's time zone.

household-setup.choose-country.note: The empty first choice of the country list, shown until a country is chosen.

household-setup.time-zone.note: Label of the household's time zone: one of the chosen country's, such as 'Brussels (Central European Time)'.

household-setup.language.note: Label of the household's language, which people invited to it start with (ADR-0016 §2). Each language is listed in its own name.

household-setup.language-hint.note: Hint under the household's language, which differs from the head's own (ADR-0016 §2).

household-setup.week-start.note: Label of the household's week start day, a list of weekday names; Monday unless changed (ADR-0007 §2).

household-setup.you.note: Heading of the group of the head's own fields: their name and language, their age, and the terms.

household-setup.your-name.note: Label of the head's name, which becomes their account's name and their profile's in the household (ADR-0007 §2, clarification).

household-setup.your-language.note: Label of the language the head reads the app in, which can differ from the household's (ADR-0007 §2, clarification). Each language is listed in its own name.

household-setup.adult.note: Checkbox: only an adult creates a household (ADR-0010 §1). A plain statement, not a question.

household-setup.terms.note: Checkbox, only on an instance that has its own terms (ADR-0007 §2, clarification). The link below it opens them. Also on the form where someone invited creates their account (ADR-0010 §1, clarification).

household-setup.read-terms.note: Link under the terms checkbox to the instance's terms, which open in a new tab so the form stays as it is. Also on the form where someone invited creates their account.

household-setup.passkey.note: Above the button that creates the household: the account is secured with a passkey, which the device asks for next (ADR-0010 §3).

household-setup.create.note: The step's button: the device makes a passkey, then the household and the account are created.

household-setup.unsupported.note: In place of the button, in a browser without JavaScript or without passkeys. Calm: the link from the e-mail still works in another browser.

household-setup.failed.note: Heading of the box at the top of the step that says why the household wasn't created.

household-setup.check.note: Leads to the list of fields that need changing, each a link to its field.

household-setup.not-created.note: When making the passkey was cancelled or refused, or creating the household failed. Calm: nothing was stored, and the link still works.

household-setup.invalid-name.note: Next to the household's name, and in the summary, when it is empty or too long.

household-setup.invalid-country.note: Next to the country, and in the summary, when none of the list is chosen.

household-setup.invalid-time-zone.note: Next to the time zone, and in the summary, when it isn't one of the chosen country's.

household-setup.invalid-language.note: Next to the household's language, and in the summary, when it isn't one of the offered ones.

household-setup.invalid-week-start.note: Next to the week start day, and in the summary, when it isn't a day of the week.

household-setup.invalid-head-name.note: Next to the head's name, and in the summary, when it is empty or too long.

household-setup.invalid-head-language.note: Next to the head's language, and in the summary, when it isn't one of the offered ones.

household-setup.invalid-adult.note: Next to the age checkbox, and in the summary, when it isn't ticked (ADR-0010 §1). States the rule without blame.

household-setup.invalid-terms.note: Next to the terms checkbox, and in the summary, when it isn't ticked.

email.sign-up.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail with a link to sign up (ADR-0010 §1). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.sign-up.request.note: First line of the sign-up e-mail. It doesn't say who asked: anyone can type any address.

email.sign-up.action.note: Text of the link in the sign-up e-mail, and the label before the link in its plain-text part.

email.sign-up.expiry.note: Says how long the sign-up link works (ADR-0010 §1, clarification: 30 minutes).

email.sign-up.not-you.note: Last line of the sign-up e-mail, for someone who didn't ask. Calm: nothing happens unless the link is used.

home.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the page listing the households an account belongs to.

home.title.note: Heading of the page listing the households an account belongs to, and the link to it.

home.none.note: Shown on that page when the account belongs to no household.

home.invitation.note: Follows home.none: how to join a household. Invitations are links a head shares.

household.page-title.note: Browser tab title of a household's page. {name} is the household's name.

household.members.note: Heading of the list of the household's members.

household.you.note: The signed-in person's own entry in the list of members. {name} is their name.

household.head.note: Role of a member who manages the household (its settings, members and plans).

household.adult.note: Role of an adult member who isn't a head.

household.add-adult.note: Heading of the form on a household's page where a head adds an adult member's profile.

household.add-adult-intro.note: Explains the form: the profile is a member at once, and the person can link an account to it later through an invitation.

household.name.note: Label of the name field of the person being added.

household.added.note: Shown once a profile is added. {name} is its name. The head is asked to tell that person, who can see what is recorded about them once they join (GDPR transparency).

household.add-failed.note: Heading of the error summary when adding a profile didn't work.

household.invalid-name.note: Why adding didn't work: no name, or one over 100 characters. 'Their' is gender-neutral.

household.invite.note: Button on a household's page that makes an invitation link for the profile of {name}, an adult without an account yet.

household.new-link.note: Button that replaces {name}'s invitation link with a new one; the old one stops working.

household.revoke.note: Button that revokes {name}'s invitation link so it no longer works.

household.link.note: Label of the read-only field holding the invitation link just made for {name}.

household.link-help.note: Under the invitation link: the link works once and for 7 days; anyone who opens it can join as that profile, so it must only go to that person.

household.link-out.note: Shown for a profile whose invitation link was made earlier and still works, with the whole days left.

household.copy.note: Button that copies the invitation link to the clipboard.

household.copied.note: Status once the link is copied.

household.revoked.note: Status once {name}'s invitation link is revoked.

household.not-invitable.note: Why no link was made: the profile has an account by now, or is gone.

household.joined-as.note: Shown to heads under a member who accepted an invitation: the name and e-mail address of the account that accepted it, so a head can tell if the wrong person did.

invitation.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the page an invitation link opens.

invitation.title.note: Heading of that page. {household} is the household's name.

invitation.title-expired.note: Heading of that page when the link no longer works.

invitation.invited.note: What the invitation is for. {household} is the household's name, {profile} the name the head gave the person's profile.

invitation.sign-in-first.note: On the invitation page, for someone not signed in: they can sign in, or create an account (after confirming their e-mail address).

invitation.sign-in.note: Link to the sign-in page, which comes back to the invitation.

invitation.accept.note: Button that accepts the invitation and joins the household.

invitation.failed.note: Heading of the error summary when accepting didn't work.

invitation.member.note: Why accepting didn't work: the account already belongs to that household.

invitation.not-allowed.note: Why accepting didn't work: the account's e-mail address isn't confirmed yet.

invitation.expired.note: Shown when the link has expired, was used, revoked or replaced.

invitation.create-account.note: Link to the sign-up page, for someone invited who has no account yet.

invitation.confirmed.note: Shown once the person confirmed their address with a sign-up link and came back to the invitation. {email} is that address.

invitation.your-name.note: Label of the new account's name; it starts as the name the head gave the profile.

invitation.your-language.note: Label of the new account's own language.

invitation.passkey.note: Explains that the account signs in with a passkey.

invitation.join-with-passkey.note: Button that creates the account with a passkey and joins the household.

invitation.unsupported.note: Shown instead of the button where the browser can't make a passkey or JavaScript is off.

invitation.check.note: Error summary message when fields need changing; the fields follow as links.

invitation.not-created.note: Error summary message when the passkey wasn't made or was refused.

invitation.sign-up-expired.note: Error when the sign-up link stopped working while the form was filled in.

invitation.ask-again.note: Link to ask for a new sign-up link.

invitation.invalid-terms.note: Why the form was refused: the terms weren't accepted. Uses the same verb as the checkbox (household-setup.terms).

household.share.note: Button that opens the device's share sheet with the invitation link (only where the browser has one).

household.share-title.note: Title of the shared invitation, as messaging apps show it. {household} is the household's name.

household.share-text.note: Text that goes with the shared invitation link. {household} is the household's name.

household.qr-help.note: Above the QR code: the invited person can scan it with their phone's camera. {name} is the profile's name.

household.qr.note: Accessible name of the QR code image. {name} is the profile's name.

household.add-child.note: Heading of the form on a household's page where a head adds a child's profile (a member under 18).

household.add-child-intro.note: Explains who may add a child: only an adult with parental responsibility, who consents for the child (GDPR art. 8). Someone without it, such as a step-parent, asks a parent to add the child. 'Parental responsibility' is the legal term ('ouderlijk gezag').

household.birth-date.note: Label of the child's birth date field, a date picker.

household.child-consent.note: DRAFT, awaiting approval. Checkbox the head ticks to add a child: they confirm they hold parental responsibility and consent to the child's use of the app (ADR-0010 §9). The exact sentence the head sees is stored as the proof of their consent, so it must read as a plain statement in the first person, and changing it changes what later records keep.

household.child-added.note: Shown once a child's profile is added. {name} is the child's name. The head is asked to tell the child, in a way a child understands, that they can see what is recorded about them once they have an account (GDPR transparency). 'Them' is one child, gender-neutral.

household.check.note: Leads to the list of the child's fields that need changing, each a link to its field.

household.invalid-birth-date.note: Next to the birth date, and in the summary, when it isn't a date, or is a date still to come. 'Their' is gender-neutral.

household.child-is-adult.note: Next to the birth date, and in the summary, when the person is 18 or older: an adult, whom the form above adds. States the rule without blame.

household.invalid-consent.note: Next to the consent checkbox, and in the summary, when it isn't ticked. States the rule without blame.

household.more.note: Accessible name of the navigation at the bottom of a household's page (settings, activity, security).

household.settings.note: Link to the household's settings, for heads.

household.activity.note: Link to the household's activity log, for every member.

settings.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the household settings page.

settings.title.note: Heading of the household settings page.

settings.country-hint.note: Under the country: the country decides the digital consent age, from which a child can have their own account.

settings.logged.note: Above the save button: changes show in the household's activity log, which every member sees (without the new values).

settings.save.note: Button that saves the household's settings.

settings.failed.note: Heading of the error summary when saving didn't work.

settings.conflict.note: Another head ({name}) saved the settings after this form was loaded, so nothing was saved; the person's input stays in the form.

settings.conflict-someone.note: Same as settings.conflict, when it isn't known who changed them.

settings.current.note: Heading of the list of the settings as they are now, shown with a conflict.

settings.back.note: Link back to the household's page.

activity.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the household's activity log.

activity.title.note: Heading of the household's activity log.

activity.intro.note: Explains the activity log: actions that affect others, visible to every member, never changed or deleted.

activity.none.note: Shown when the log is empty.

activity.former-member.note: Stands for {actor} in the entries when the person is no longer a member. Starts with a capital, as it begins the sentence.

activity.household-name.note: Log entry. {actor} is a member's name, or 'A former member'. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.household-country.note: Log entry. {actor} is a member's name, or 'A former member'. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.household-time-zone.note: Log entry. {actor} is a member's name, or 'A former member'. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.household-language.note: Log entry. {actor} is a member's name, or 'A former member'. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

time-zone.name.note: A time zone in a list or a summary, such as 'Brussels (Central European Time)'. {city} is the last part of the zone's IANA name, not translated; {zone} is the zone's name from the browser, already in the reader's language, or an offset such as 'GMT+03:00'.

household.shares.note: Link from the household page to its shares page.

shares.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the shares page.

shares.title.note: Heading of the page where heads set how much of the household's work each member does.

shares.intro.note: Explains shares (ADR-0001 §4). 'Share' is the member's portion of the work, not a share in a company.

shares.private-heads.note: Shown to heads: who sees shares (ADR-0018 §4).

shares.private.note: Shown to members who aren't heads: who sees their share (ADR-0018 §4).

shares.private-child.note: Shown to children: who sees their share (ADR-0018 §4, ADR-0012 §3). 'Parents' are the members with parental responsibility for the child.

shares.default.note: A member's share this week, which is the default for an adult. {share} is a formatted percentage, such as 100%.

shares.by-age.note: A child's share this week, by their age. {share} is a formatted percentage, such as 36%.

shares.set.note: A share a head set instead of the default. {share} is a formatted percentage, such as 50%.

shares.hint.note: Hint under the share fields. {min} and {max} are numbers, such as 0 and 100.

shares.field.note: Label of the field for a member's share, in percent. {name} is the member's name.

shares.save.note: Button that saves a member's share.

shares.use-default.note: Button that puts a member's share back to the default by role and age.

shares.saved.note: Status after saving a member's share.

shares.failed.note: Heading of the error summary when a share wasn't saved.

shares.check.note: Error summary message when the share entered isn't valid.

shares.invalid.note: Why a share wasn't accepted, next to its field and in the error summary. {min} and {max} are numbers, such as 0 and 100.

shares.conflict.note: Shown when someone changed the member since the page was loaded (ADR-0019 §5). {name} is the member's name, {share} a formatted percentage.

shares.temporary-this-week.note: A member's share this week when a temporary share covers some of its days. {share} is a formatted percentage, such as 43%.

shares.temporary-list.note: Accessible name of the list of a member's temporary shares.

shares.temporary.note: A temporary share. {share} is a formatted percentage, such as 50%; {days} a formatted range of days, such as 12–18 October 2026.

shares.remove-temporary.note: Button that removes a temporary share. {share} is a formatted percentage, {days} a formatted range of days.

shares.add-temporary.note: Opens the form that adds a temporary share for a member.

shares.temporary-hint.note: Hint of the form that adds a temporary share (ADR-0001 §4, ADR-0012 §2: no reason is stored).

shares.first-day.note: Label of the first day of a temporary share.

shares.last-day.note: Label of the last day of a temporary share.

shares.temporary-field.note: Label of the share of a temporary share, in percent.

shares.add-temporary-button.note: Button that adds the temporary share.

shares.added-temporary.note: Status after adding a temporary share.

shares.removed-temporary.note: Status after removing a temporary share.

shares.check-temporary.note: Error summary message when a temporary share isn't valid.

shares.invalid-first-day.note: Why the first day of a temporary share wasn't accepted. {earliest} and {latest} are formatted dates, such as 12 October 2026.

shares.invalid-last-day.note: Why the last day of a temporary share wasn't accepted. {latest} is a formatted date.

shares.overlap.note: Shown when a new temporary share would overlap one the member has. {share} is a formatted percentage, {days} a formatted range of days.

shares.overlap-days.note: Next to the first day, when a temporary share would overlap another. {days} is a formatted range of days.

tasks.title.note: Heading of a household's task list, and the link to it from the household's page.

tasks.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the task list. {household} is the household's name; Householdr is the product name, not translated.

tasks.back.note: Link from the task list back to the household's page. {household} is the household's name.

tasks.none.note: Shown instead of the task list while the household has no tasks.

tasks.how-often.note: Label of a task's frequency in the list, and of the field that chooses it when adding or changing a task.

tasks.how-long.note: Label of how long one time of a task takes, in the list and where a task is shown as it is now. The value next to it is a number of minutes.

tasks.if-not-done.note: Label, in the task list and where a task is shown as it is now, of what happens to a time of the task that isn't done (ADR-0002 §2). The value next to it is tasks.roll-over or tasks.lapse.

tasks.daily.note: A task's frequency, in the list and as a choice when adding or changing a task (ADR-0004 §3).

tasks.weekly.note: A task's frequency, in the list and as a choice when adding or changing a task (ADR-0004 §3).

tasks.biweekly.note: A task's frequency, in the list and as a choice when adding or changing a task (ADR-0004 §3).

tasks.monthly.note: A task's frequency, in the list and as a choice when adding or changing a task (ADR-0004 §3).

tasks.tri-monthly.note: A task's frequency, in the list and as a choice when adding or changing a task (ADR-0004 §3).

tasks.yearly.note: A task's frequency, in the list and as a choice when adding or changing a task (ADR-0004 §3).

tasks.add.note: Heading of the form where a head adds a task of their own to the household.

tasks.name.note: Label of the task's name field, when adding or changing a task, and of its name where it is shown as it is now.

tasks.name-hint.note: Hint under the task's name field, with an example of a task name.

tasks.duration.note: Label of the field for how many minutes one time of the task takes.

tasks.start.note: Label of the date field for the first day the task is due, when adding or changing it, and of that day where a task is shown as it is now.

tasks.start-hint.note: Hint under the first-time date field: later times are counted from it, by the chosen frequency.

tasks.on-miss.note: Heading (legend) of the two choices for what happens to a time of the task that isn't done in its week or window (ADR-0002 §2), when adding or changing it.

tasks.roll-over.note: Choice, and its value in the task list: a time that isn't done stays open and goes into the next week's work, like cleaning the bathroom (ADR-0002 §2). The form starts on it. Calm: nobody is blamed.

tasks.lapse.note: Choice, and its value in the task list: a time that isn't done closes, since doing it later makes no sense, like putting the bins out (ADR-0002 §2). Calm: nobody is blamed.

tasks.added.note: Shown once a task is added. {name} is the task's name, as typed.

tasks.add-failed.note: Heading of the error summary when adding a task didn't work.

tasks.check.note: Leads to the list of fields that need changing when adding or saving a task, each a link to its field.

tasks.invalid-name.note: Why adding or saving a task didn't work: no name, or one over 100 characters.

tasks.invalid-duration.note: Why adding or saving a task didn't work: the minutes aren't a whole number in range. {min} and {max} are the fewest and most minutes allowed (1 and 1440, a day).

tasks.invalid-frequency.note: Why adding or saving a task didn't work: no frequency chosen.

tasks.invalid-start.note: Why adding didn't work: the first time is not a day from today up to a year from today.

tasks.invalid-on-miss.note: Why adding or saving a task didn't work: neither choice for what happens to a time that isn't done was picked.

tasks.edit.note: Link next to each task in the list, for heads, to the page that changes or removes it. Screen readers read it with the task's name after it.

tasks.removed.note: Shown on the task list after a head removed a task on its own page.

task.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the page that changes a task. {task} is the task's name, {household} the household's; Householdr is the product name, not translated.

task.title.note: Heading of the page where a head changes a task: its name, minutes, frequency, first time and what happens if it isn't done.

task.save.note: Button that saves the changes to the task.

task.saved.note: Shown once the changes to a task are saved.

task.failed.note: Heading of the error summary when saving a task didn't work: a field was refused, or someone changed the task in the meantime.

task.conflict.note: Why saving didn't work: another head (or the same one in another tab) saved the task after this form was opened (ADR-0019 §5). Nothing is lost: the form keeps what was typed. Calm, nobody is blamed.

task.current.note: Heading above the task as it is saved now, shown when it changed since the form was opened, to compare with the form.

task.invalid-start.note: Why saving didn't work: the first time is a day in the past other than the one the task already has, or more than a year away. A task that has started keeps its first time.

task.remove.note: Link from the page that changes a task to the page that asks to confirm removing it.

task.back.note: Link from a task's page back to the household's task list.

task.remove-page-title.note: Browser tab title of the page that asks to confirm removing a task. {task} is the task's name, {household} the household's; Householdr is the product name, not translated.

task.remove-title.note: Heading of the page that asks a head to confirm removing a task. {task} is the task's name, as typed.

task.remove-intro.note: Under the question whether to remove a task: removing can't be undone.

task.remove-confirm.note: Button that removes the task, after the head was asked to confirm.

task.keep.note: Link that goes back to the task's page without removing it.

task.remove-failed.note: Heading of the error summary when removing a task didn't work, as someone changed it in the meantime.

task.remove-conflict.note: Why removing didn't work: someone saved the task after this page was opened (ADR-0019 §5), so the head confirms again with what it is now. Calm, nobody is blamed.

comparisons.title.note: Heading of the comparison game's page, where a member says which of two tasks is harder for them, and the link to it from the household's page.

comparisons.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the comparison game. {household} is the household's name; Householdr is the product name, not translated.

comparisons.why.note: Why the game is there, below the heading. Plain and reassuring, also for children: the app shows a member's answers to nobody else, heads included (ADR-0003 §5, ADR-0007 §5).

comparisons.question.note: The question above two buttons, each with a task's name. Harder means more effort, or more draining, for this person.

comparisons.skip.note: Button that moves on to another pair of tasks without answering, for when the member can't choose or finds them about the same. Nothing is saved.

comparisons.answered.note: Status after an answer. {harder} and {easier} are the names of the two tasks, as typed.

comparisons.not-saved.note: Heading of the box that says an answer didn't go through, which happens when a task was changed or removed while the page was open.

comparisons.changed.note: Below 'Your answer wasn't saved'. The page shows another pair of tasks right after it.

comparisons.none.note: Shown instead of the question while the household has fewer than two tasks.

comparisons.order.note: Heading of the list of the member's own tasks, from the one they find hardest to the one they find easiest, which their answers change. It shows no numbers (ADR-0003 §5).

comparisons.order-none.note: Shown instead of the list until the member has answered at least one question.

comparisons.order-hint.note: Above the list. Higher means harder for this member; a task that is harder for them weighs more when the weekly plans divide the tasks. No numbers on purpose.

comparisons.back.note: Link from the comparison game back to the household's page. {household} is the household's name.

availability.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the page that shows who in the household is away when. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

availability.title.note: Heading of the page that shows who in the household is away when, and the household page's link to it.

availability.intro.note: Introduces the page. Others see only that someone is away, as dates; no reason or place is ever asked (ADR-0018 §3).

availability.none.note: Under a member's name, when they have no days away coming up.

availability.first-day.note: The first day someone is away: the label of the date field, and next to that date in the list. That day is included.

availability.last-day.note: The last day someone is away: the label of the date field, and next to that date in the list. That day is included too.

availability.plan.note: Heading of the form, under a member's name, that adds days away for them: for yourself, or as a head for a child or a member without an account.

availability.add.note: The button that adds the days away.

availability.remove.note: The button next to days away that removes them.

availability.added.note: Status message once days away are added.

availability.removed.note: Status message once days away are removed.

availability.already-removed.note: Status message when someone else removed the days away a moment earlier.

availability.add-failed.note: Heading of the error summary when the days away weren't added.

availability.check.note: Introduces the list of fields to change in the error summary.

availability.invalid-first-day.note: Why the first day wasn't accepted: not a date, in the past, or more than a year ahead.

availability.invalid-last-day.note: Why the last day wasn't accepted: not a date, before the first day, or more than a year ahead.

availability.household.note: Heading of the household's time away together (ADR-0005 §5).

availability.household-intro.note: Explains what time away together does (ADR-0005 §5).

availability.household-none.note: Shown when the household has no time away together planned.

availability.household-plan.note: Legend of the form where a head plans time when the whole household is away.

availability.cant-legend.note: Legend of the form, under a member's name, where they say they can't today (ADR-0005 §3): for yourself, or as a head for a child or a member without an account.

availability.cant-intro.note: Explains “I can't today” (ADR-0005 §3): the fair portion shrinks by that time, so it's an absence, not a deficit (ADR-0002 §1); others see only the days (ADR-0018 §3). No reason is asked. Kind and plain, never guilt (UI-24).

availability.cant-last-day.note: Label of the choice of the last day someone can't: today, or a later day of this plan week, each written as a weekday and date. Read together with the chosen day.

availability.cant-today-option.note: The first choice of the last day someone can't, chosen to begin with: the end of today.

availability.i-cant.note: Button that says you can't, until the end of the day chosen (ADR-0005 §3). One tap, so short.

availability.they-cant.note: Button with which a head says a child or a member without an account, {name}, can't, until the end of the day chosen (ADR-0005 §3).

availability.cant-today.note: Under a member's name, which everyone sees: they said they can't, until the end of today. Never why (ADR-0018 §3).

availability.cant-until.note: Under a member's name, which everyone sees: they said they can't, up to the end of {day}, a weekday and date such as “Friday 9 October”. Never why (ADR-0018 §3).

availability.i-can.note: Button that ends your “I can't” now (ADR-0005 §3, clarification).

availability.they-can.note: Button with which a head ends the “can't” of a child or a member without an account, {name}, now.

availability.unavailable.note: Status message once someone said they can't (ADR-0005 §3, ADR-0018 §3).

availability.available.note: Status message once someone said they can after all.

availability.already-available.note: Status message when the “can't” had ended by itself, or someone else ended it a moment earlier.

availability.cant-invalid-day.note: Why the last day wasn't accepted, next to its field: usually one that passed while the page was open.

plan.title.note: Heading of the page with the week's plan, and the link to it on the household's page (ADR-0006).

plan.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the plan's page. {household} is the household's name.

plan.intro.note: Introduces the plan's page (ADR-0007 §5: each assignment says why it went to them).

plan.none.note: Shown instead of a plan when there is none this week or next that the reader may see.

plan.this-week.note: Heading of this week's plan. {days} is the week's first and last day, such as “12–18 October 2026”.

plan.next-week.note: Heading of next week's plan. {days} is the week's first and last day, such as “19–25 October 2026”.

plan.draft.note: Shown to heads above a draft plan (ADR-0006 §2). {when} is a day and time, such as “Sunday 11 October 2026 at 12:00”.

plan.publish.note: Button with which a head publishes the draft early, so everyone sees it (ADR-0006 §2).

plan.published.note: Status message after a head published the draft.

plan.changed.note: When a head publishes a draft that was drafted again in the meantime: nothing was published (ADR-0019 §5).

plan.gone.note: When a head publishes a draft that is gone, as for a week the household is now away all of.

plan.any-time.note: Explains once, above the plan, that a task can be done any day of the week it is in (ADR-0004 §4).

plan.day.note: Label, in a task of the plan, of the day it is planned for.

plan.any-day-this-week.note: In this week's plan, instead of a day, for a task from an earlier week that can be done any day of this one.

plan.any-day-next-week.note: In next week's plan, instead of a day, for a task from an earlier week that can be done any day of that one.

plan.points-label.note: Label, in the reader's own tasks, of the points the task costs them (ADR-0001 §5).

plan.why.note: Label, in a task of the plan, of why it went to whoever has it (ADR-0007 §5).

plan.nothing.note: Under a member's name when they have no task in the week's plan.

plan.unassigned.note: Heading, for heads, of the tasks nobody could take this week (ADR-0001 §7).

plan.unassigned-intro.note: Explains to heads what happens to a task nobody could take (ADR-0001 §7, clarification). Calm, never blaming anyone.

plan.reason.lowest-relative-load.note: Why a task went to {name}, another member: the least work so far for their share (ADR-0001 §7). Never names the share itself, which others don't see (ADR-0018 §4).

plan.reason.lowest-relative-load-you.note: Why a task went to the reader: the least work so far for their share (ADR-0001 §7).

plan.reason.only-eligible.note: Why a task went to {name}: nobody else was available or allowed (ADR-0001 §7).

plan.reason.only-eligible-you.note: Why a task went to the reader: nobody else was available or allowed (ADR-0001 §7).

plan.reason.catching-up.note: Why a task went to whoever has it: it evens out the balances of earlier weeks (ADR-0001 §7, ADR-0002 §3). Never blaming: catching up isn't a punishment.

plan.reason.bound.note: Why a task went to {name}: it is always theirs (ADR-0001 §7, bound).

plan.reason.bound-you.note: Why a task went to the reader: it is always theirs (ADR-0001 §7, bound).

plan.reason.assigned-by-head.note: Why a task went to {name}: a head of the household chose them (ADR-0001 §7).

plan.reason.assigned-by-head-you.note: Why a task went to the reader: a head of the household chose them (ADR-0001 §7).

plan.reason.linked.note: Why a task went to {name}: it goes with a task they had before, such as bringing a bin in after putting it out (ADR-0001 §7).

plan.reason.linked-you.note: Why a task went to the reader: it goes with a task they had before (ADR-0001 §7).

plan.reason.reallocated.note: Why a task went to {name}: it moved to them in this week's plan because the member who had it said they can't today, without naming that member (ADR-0005 §3, ADR-0001 §7).

plan.reason.reallocated-you.note: Why a task went to the reader: it moved to them in this week's plan because the member who had it said they can't today, without naming that member (ADR-0005 §3, ADR-0001 §7).

plan.cause.nobody-eligible.note: Why nobody has a task, for heads (ADR-0001 §7, clarification).

plan.cause.bound-member-not-eligible.note: Why nobody has a task, for heads: whoever it always goes to isn't available (ADR-0001 §7, clarification).

plan.cause.linked-member-not-eligible.note: Why nobody has a task, for heads: whoever had the task it goes with isn't available (ADR-0001 §7, clarification).

plan.back.note: Link from the plan back to the household's page. {household} is the household's name.

plan.points.note: The points a task costs the reader (ADR-0001 §5): roughly a minute of average work each.

plan.publish-failed.note: Heading of the summary when a head's publishing didn't go through; plan.changed or plan.gone says why.

household.start-title.note: Heading of the box on the household's page that leads a head to Start, the last step of setting up, while the household is in setup (ADR-0007 §2 step 7).

household.start-intro.note: Under 'Ready to start?' on the household's page, for heads while the household is in setup (ADR-0007 §2).

household.start.note: Link, styled as a button, from the household's page to the Start page.

household.started.note: Status on the household's page right after a head started it on the week start day (ADR-0007 §3). {week} is a day such as “Monday 12 October”; {draft} and {publish} are a day and time such as “Sunday 11 October 2026 at 12:00”.

activity.household-started.note: Log entry when a head started the household, which ends setting it up (ADR-0007 §2). {actor} is a member's name, or 'A former member'. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.set-before-start.note: Follows 'started the household' when a head had set shares, and planned days away for members without an account, before the start (ADR-0018 §5). Never shows a value. {shares} and {daysAway} are lists of names, such as “Sam and Kim”.

activity.set-before-start-shares.note: As 'Set before the start: shares for …; days away for …', when only shares were set. {shares} is a list of names, such as “Sam and Kim”.

activity.set-before-start-days-away.note: As 'Set before the start: shares for …; days away for …', when only days away were planned. {daysAway} is a list of names, such as “Sam”.

activity.a-former-member.note: Stands for a name in the lists of 'Set before the start' when the person is no longer a member. Lower case, as it sits in a sentence.

activity.you.note: Stands for the reader in the lists of 'Set before the start', such as “you and Sam” (ADR-0018 §5, clarification). Lower case, as it sits in a sentence; in Dutch the object form, “jou”.

plan.draft-heads-publish.note: Shown to heads above the draft of this week's plan when a household has just started (ADR-0007 §3): nothing publishes it on its own, a head does.

start.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the Start page, the last step of setting up a household (ADR-0007 §2 step 7).

start.intro.note: Introduces the two ways to start a household (ADR-0007 §3).

start.when.note: Legend of the two choices on the Start page.

start.now.note: The first choice, chosen unless the head picks the other (ADR-0007 §2).

start.now-hint.note: Explains 'Start now' (ADR-0007 §3). {last} is the last day of this week, such as “Sunday 11 October”.

start.week-start.note: The second choice: start on the household's week start day. {day} is that day, such as “Monday 12 October”.

start.week-start-hint.note: Explains starting on the week start day (ADR-0007 §3). {draft} and {publish} are a day and time, such as “Saturday 10 October 2026 at 00:00”.

start.failed.note: Heading of the error summary on the Start page.

start.invalid.note: When the form came without a choice.

start.already-started.note: When another head started the household while this one was choosing. Calm: the household has started.

start.started.note: On the Start page when it is opened after the household started.

activity.completion-logged.note: An entry of the activity log: someone marked a task done that {subject} is credited for, on their behalf or done together (ADR-0018 §5). {subject} is a name or 'a former member'. Never which task or its points. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.completion-undone.note: An entry of the activity log: someone undid a task that {subject} was credited for (ADR-0006 §4, ADR-0018 §5). {subject} is a name or 'a former member'. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

plan.you.note: Stands for the reader in the lists of who did a task and who logged it, as in 'Done on Thursday 15 October by you and Alex'. Lower case, as it sits in a sentence after 'by'.

plan.a-former-member.note: Someone who did or logged a task and has since left the household, in the middle of a sentence such as 'Done today by a former member.' (ADR-0012 §6).

plan.done.note: Under a task that is done: when it was done and who did it. {day} is 'today', 'yesterday' or 'on Monday' (see plan.done-today and the next ones); {doers} is a list such as 'Alex' or 'you and Kim'. Others see the day only, never the time (ADR-0018 §3).

plan.done-at.note: Under a task that is done, for those who did it only: when it was done, the time of day in the household's time zone, and who did it. {day} is 'today', 'yesterday' or 'on Monday', as in plan.done; {doers} is a list such as 'you' or 'you and Kim' (ADR-0018 §3).

plan.logged-by.note: Under a task that is done, when whoever marked it done wasn't the only one who did it: who marked it done, by name or 'you' (ADR-0002, Consequences).

plan.undo.note: Button under someone else's task that is done, which marks it as not done again. Shown to whoever marked it done, those who did it, and heads, until the end of the week (ADR-0006 §4). The reader's own task unticks its box instead.

plan.undo-label.note: What screen readers call the Undo button: it starts with plan.undo, then names the task and its day (weekday, day and month), so each button on the page has a name of its own.

plan.done-button.note: Visible text next to the box at the end of the reader's own task in this week's plan, which ticks it done with one tap and unticks it to undo it (ADR-0006 §4). Short, as it says the reader did it.

plan.done-label.note: What screen readers call the box on the reader's own task, ticked or not: it starts with plan.done-button, then names the task and its day (weekday, day and month).

plan.done-with-others.note: Opens a choice of who did the reader's own task: with others, or someone else instead of them (ADR-0006 §4).

plan.mark-done.note: Opens a choice of who did a task of someone else's, or of nobody's: whoever it was given to, the reader picking it up, or several together (ADR-0006 §4, ADR-0002 §4). Differs from plan.mark-done-button, the choice's own button.

plan.who.note: Heading of the list of household members to tick who did a task. Several can be ticked: each gets the task's points (ADR-0002 §1).

plan.mark-done-button.note: Button under the list of who did a task, which marks it done for those ticked.

plan.mark-done-label.note: What screen readers call the button under the list of who did a task: it starts with plan.mark-done-button, then names the task and its day (weekday, day and month).

plan.no-doers.note: Next to the list of who did a task, when it was sent with nobody ticked.

plan.no-doers-summary.note: In the summary at the top of the week when a task was sent to be marked done with nobody ticked; links to the list. {task} is the task's name as the household typed it.

plan.complete-failed.note: Heading of the summary when marking a task done didn't go through; the message under it says why.

plan.undo-failed.note: Heading of the summary when undoing a task that was done didn't go through; the message under it says why.

plan.already-done.note: When someone else marked the task done a moment before the reader (ADR-0019 §6). {doers} is who did it, a list such as 'Alex' or 'you and Kim'. Calm, never a reproach.

plan.not-completable.note: When a task can no longer be marked done: its week is over, or it was taken out of the plan. The page shows the plan as it is now.

plan.week-over.note: When undoing a task that was done comes after the end of its plan week (ADR-0006 §4).

plan.undone-already.note: When someone else undid the task a moment before the reader tried to.

plan.completed.note: Read out after the reader marked a task done (UI-12). {task} is the task's name as the household typed it.

plan.reopened.note: Read out after the reader undid a task that was done: it is to be done again (UI-12).

activity.completion-picked-up.note: Activity log entry: {actor} did a task the plan gave to {subject}, so it became their work (a pick-up). {actor} and {subject} are names, or “a former member”; the task and its points are never shown. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

household.balances.note: Link from the household page to the balances page, for every member.

balances.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the balances page. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

balances.title.note: Heading of the page with every member's balance (ADR-0002 §6): how far ahead of or behind their fair portion of the work each member is, in points.

balances.intro.note: Explains a balance (ADR-0002 §1): what someone did compared with their fair portion of the work. Neutral words: being behind is never a fault (UI-24).

balances.evening-out.note: Explains catching up (ADR-0002 §3): the coming plans give a bit more to whoever is behind and a bit less to whoever is ahead.

balances.rate-fast.note: The household's rebalance rate, set by a head (ADR-0002 §3): fast. 'Them' are the balances.

balances.rate-normal.note: The household's rebalance rate, set by a head (ADR-0002 §3): normal, the default. 'Them' are the balances.

balances.rate-slow.note: The household's rebalance rate, set by a head (ADR-0002 §3): slow. 'Them' are the balances.

balances.points.note: A balance, or what one week changed it by, in whole points (ADR-0001 §5). {points} is the number with its sign, such as “+12”, “-30” or “0”; {count} picks the plural.

balances.history.note: Caption of a member's table of weeks, newest first, each with what it changed their balance by.

balances.week.note: Column heading: the plan week, such as “12–18 October 2026”.

balances.change.note: Column heading: what that week changed the balance by, in points.

balances.no-history.note: Shown instead of the table of weeks until the household's first week is over and counted.

plan.joined-since.note: For heads, on a draft: who joined the household after the draft was made, by name as a list (count is how many), so the draft gives them no tasks and they owe nothing for that week (ADR-0002 §1, clarification). It suggests drafting it again.

plan.redraft.note: Button under plan.joined-since: a head makes the draft again, which replaces it and shares the work with everyone in the household now.

plan.redrafted.note: Status once a head made a draft again.

plan.redraft-failed.note: Heading of the summary when making a draft again didn't go through; plan.redraft-gone says why.

plan.redraft-gone.note: Why a head couldn't make a draft again: another head published it meanwhile.

activity.share-changed.note: Activity log entry, after the household started: a head set {subject}’s share, or put it back to the default; {subject} can be the head themselves (ADR-0018 §4–§5). {actor} and {subject} are names, or “a former member”. Never the share itself, which only heads and the member see. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.temporary-share-added.note: Activity log entry, after the household started: a head planned a temporary share for {subject}, a share for a few days or weeks (ADR-0001 §4). {actor} and {subject} are names, or “a former member”. Never its days or the share. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.temporary-share-removed.note: Activity log entry, after the household started: a head removed one of {subject}’s temporary shares. {actor} and {subject} are names, or “a former member”. Never which one. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.absence-added.note: Activity log entry, after the household started: a head planned days away for {subject}, a member without an account, acting for them (ADR-0018 §5). “Days away” as on the availability page. {actor} and {subject} are names, or “a former member”. Never the days. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.absence-removed.note: Activity log entry, after the household started: a head removed days away planned for {subject}, a member without an account. {actor} and {subject} are names, or “a former member”. Never the days. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.unavailable-reported.note: Activity log entry, after the household started: a head said {subject}, a member without an account, can't today, acting for them (ADR-0005 §3, ADR-0018 §5). “Can't today” as on the availability page, also when it lasts to a later day. {actor} and {subject} are names, or “a former member”. Never until when or why. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.unavailable-ended.note: Activity log entry, after the household started: a head said {subject}, a member without an account, can after all, ending their “can't today” (ADR-0005 §3, clarification; ADR-0018 §5). {actor} and {subject} are names, or “a former member”. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

past.today.note: The day something happened: today. One step of the scale of how long ago a day was (ADR-0008 §6, clarification), never finer than the day (ADR-0018 §3); the exact day shows in a tooltip. Starts with a capital, as it stands alone.

past.yesterday.note: The day something happened: yesterday. One step of the scale of how long ago a day was (ADR-0008 §6, clarification), never finer than the day (ADR-0018 §3); the exact day shows in a tooltip. Starts with a capital, as it stands alone.

past.some-days-ago.note: The day something happened: two to six days ago. One step of the scale of how long ago a day was (ADR-0008 §6, clarification), never finer than the day (ADR-0018 §3); the exact day shows in a tooltip. Starts with a capital, as it stands alone.

past.last-week.note: The day something happened: in the household's plan week before this one, a week or more ago. One step of the scale of how long ago a day was (ADR-0008 §6, clarification), never finer than the day (ADR-0018 §3); the exact day shows in a tooltip. Starts with a capital, as it stands alone.

past.some-weeks-ago.note: The day something happened: before last week, less than five weeks ago; longer ago, the date itself shows. One step of the scale of how long ago a day was (ADR-0008 §6, clarification), never finer than the day (ADR-0018 §3); the exact day shows in a tooltip. Starts with a capital, as it stands alone.

plan.done-today.note: {day} in 'Done {day} by …' when it was done today. Lower case, as it sits in the sentence; the exact day shows in a tooltip.

plan.done-yesterday.note: {day} in 'Done {day} by …' when it was done yesterday. Lower case, as it sits in the sentence.

plan.done-on.note: {day} in 'Done {day} by …' earlier this plan week. {weekday} is the day of the week, such as 'Monday'.

activity.away-added.note: Activity log entry: a head marked the whole household away for a time, such as a family holiday ('Time away together' on the availability page; ADR-0005 §5). {actor} is a name, or “A former member”. Never the days. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

activity.away-removed.note: Activity log entry: a head removed a time the whole household is away. {actor} is a name, or “A former member”. Never the days. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

leave.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the page where a member leaves the household {household} (ADR-0005 §4, ADR-0018 §2).

leave.title.note: Heading of that page. {household} is the household's name.

leave.failed.note: Heading of the error summary when leaving didn't go through.

leave.invalid.note: Leaving was sent without a choice of how the history shows the member.

leave.last-adult.note: Shown instead of the form to the household's last head when no other adult with an account is left: leaving would close the household, which isn't built yet (ADR-0018 §2, clarification). Plain, without blame.

leave.successor-gone.note: Leaving didn't go through because the member the last head chose to become head has left, or can no longer become head, meanwhile (ADR-0018 §2, clarification).

leave.last-head.note: Above the choice of who becomes head, for the household's last head: the head role passes as they leave (ADR-0018 §2, clarification). Plain, without blame.

leave.intro.note: What leaving does: it is immediate, no reason is asked, and nobody is notified (ADR-0018 §2, §8). Quiet and reassuring.

leave.history.note: What stays and what moves when a member leaves: their history and frozen balance stay, their open tasks go to the others (ADR-0005 §4).

leave.rejoin.note: Someone who left comes back only through a new invitation they accept themselves (ADR-0018 §2).

leave.successor.note: Legend of the last head's choice of who becomes head when they leave (ADR-0018 §2, clarification).

leave.successor-rule.note: First choice, chosen to begin with: naming no one, which gives the head role to the adult with an account who has been in the household longest, {name} (ADR-0018 §2). The other choices are the members' names.

leave.successor-decline.note: Under that choice: a member the leaving head names is asked later whether they take it on; if they decline, the role goes to the adult with an account longest in the household after them (ADR-0018 §2, clarification).

leave.shown-as.note: Legend of the choice of how the household's history shows the member after they leave (ADR-0018 §2, clarification).

leave.as-former.note: First choice, chosen to begin with: shown as 'Former member', the same words the history uses.

leave.as-name.note: Second choice: shown under their own name, {name}.

leave.submit.note: Button that leaves the household at once.

leave.support.note: One plain line about a support service for domestic violence in the household's country (ADR-0018 §8). {service} is its name, such as '1712' or 'Veilig Thuis', {phone} its number and {website} a link to its website. Calm and discreet: it may be read on a shared screen.

home.left.note: Status message on the list of the account's households right after leaving one.

household.leave.note: Link on the household's page to the page where the member can leave it.

household.named-head-title.note: Heading of the part of the household's page for a member the last head named head as they left, until they answer (ADR-0018 §2, clarification).

household.named-head.note: In that part: they hold the role already, and are asked whether they take it on; declining passes it to the adult with an account longest in the household after them (ADR-0018 §2, clarification). Never names the head who left.

household.named-head-only.note: In that part, instead, for the only adult with an account, who can't decline; also the status when declining was refused for that reason (ADR-0018 §2, clarification).

household.take-on.note: Button: the member takes the head role on, and isn't asked again.

household.decline-head.note: Button: the member declines the head role, which passes to someone else.

household.took-on.note: Status message after taking the head role on.

household.declined-head.note: Status message after declining the head role; the members list shows who is head now.

household.two-factors-title.note: Heading of the part of the household's page that asks a head without two factors to set them up (ADR-0010 §3, ADR-0018 §2).

household.two-factors.note: Head powers wait until the account signs in with two factors: a passkey, or a password with two-factor authentication (ADR-0010 §3, clarification). Use the security page's words for both.

household.two-factors-link.note: Link to the account's security page, where passkeys and two-factor authentication are set up.

remove.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the page where a head removes {name} from the household {household} (ADR-0005 §4, ADR-0018 §4).

remove.title.note: Heading of that page. {name} is the member being removed.

remove.intro.note: What removing does: the same as when the member leaves themselves, at once (ADR-0005 §4, clarification).

remove.history.note: What stays and what moves: their history and frozen balance stay, shown as 'Former member' (as the history words it), their open tasks go to the others.

remove.child.note: Shown when the member is a child: removing them doesn't touch their account, guardians or other households (ADR-0010 §10).

remove.logged.note: Removing a member is shown to every member in the household's activity (ADR-0018 §5). 'Activity log' as the household's page names the activity page.

remove.confirm.note: Shown instead of the button when the head signed in more than 10 minutes ago: they confirm their identity on the security page first (ADR-0010 §6).

remove.confirm-link.note: Link to the security page, where the head confirms it's them; the same words as that page's heading.

remove.keep.note: Link back to the household's page without removing {name}.

household.remove.note: Link, for heads, next to a member on the household's page, to the page that removes {name}.

household.removed.note: Status message on the household's page right after a head removed a member, who isn't named: they show as a former member now (ADR-0018 §2, clarification).

activity.member-removed.note: Activity log entry, after the household started: a head removed {subject} from the household (ADR-0005 §4, ADR-0018 §5). {actor} is a name or 'A former member'; {subject} is usually 'a former member', as someone removed shows as one until they choose otherwise. {who} picks the wording: 'you' when the reader did it, 'to-you' when it was done to the reader, 'yourself' when the reader did it to themselves, 'themselves' when {actor} did it to themselves, '*' otherwise (ADR-0018 §5, clarification).

balances.former-members.note: Heading of the balances page's part for members who left or were removed, after the current members (ADR-0005 §4, clarification).

balances.former-intro.note: Under that heading: a former member's balance is frozen, never handed on to anyone (ADR-0005 §4).

balances.former-member.note: Heading of the balance of someone who left and didn't choose to appear under their name; the same words as the leave page's choice (ADR-0018 §2, clarification).

tasks.since-last-done.note: A choice under 'How often', next to the fixed frequencies: the task is due a while after it was last done, not on set dates (for example cleaning the oven).

tasks.every.note: Heading over the two fields that say how long after the last time a task counted from when it was last done is due again.

tasks.every-count.note: Label of the number in 'Due again after', such as the 6 in 'every 6 weeks'.

tasks.every-unit.note: Label of the choice of unit in 'Due again after'.

tasks.unit-days.note: A unit to choose in 'Due again after', after the number.

tasks.unit-weeks.note: A unit to choose in 'Due again after', after the number.

tasks.unit-months.note: A unit to choose in 'Due again after', after the number.
